sections.section_name: Section B - Applied Raga & Tala Concepts

questions.question_text: Explain the structural and functional difference between a 'Peshkar' and a 'Kayada' within a traditional Tabla solo performance. [40-50 words]
questions.answer: Peshkar is a slow, highly improvised introductory composition that establishes the foundational groove and intricate Laya variations of the Tala. Kayada is a strict, rule-bound composition consisting of a basic theme that is methodically expanded through structural variations (Paltas) and logically concludes with a mathematical Tihai.

questions.question_text: Describe the physical composition and the acoustic function of the 'Syahi' (black patch) applied on the Tabla drumheads. [40-50 words]
questions.answer: The Syahi is a circular, multi-layered paste made from iron oxide powder, soot, flour, and glue. Applied to the center of the Dayan and off-center on the Bayan, it adds localized mass to the membrane, suppressing non-harmonic overtones and enabling a clear, sustained, and highly tuned metallic pitch.

questions.question_text: Differentiate between the concepts of 'Tali' and 'Khali' as navigational markers within the framework of Hindustani Tala systems. [40-50 words]
questions.answer: Tali refers to an accented, heavy beat structurally marked by a physical hand clap, highlighting the subdivisions of the rhythm. Khali represents an unaccented, empty beat marked by a silent wave of the hand, acting as a critical sonic rest point to help performers navigate the cyclic Tala.

questions.question_text: Trace the brief historical evolution and physical adaptation of the Pakhawaj from the ancient classical Mridangam. [40-50 words]
questions.answer: The Pakhawaj evolved from the ancient barrel-shaped Mridangam mentioned in the Natyashastra. During the medieval period, it was structurally refined alongside the majestic Dhrupad vocal style. It features a heavy wooden shell and utilizes freshly kneaded wheat-dough on the left head to produce a deep, resonant bass.

questions.question_text: Write the structural layout grid and full notation of Jhaptal showing its rhythmic divisions (Vibhags), claps (Tali), and wave hands (Khali) in Thah (Single) and Dugun (Double) speed configurations. [Notation structural format]
questions.answer:
Jhaptal consists of 10 Matras divided into 4 asymmetrical blocks (2-3-2-3). The Sam (Tali) is on beat 1, subsequent Talis on beats 3 and 8, and the Khali on beat 6.

Thah (Single) Layout:
| Dhi Na | Dhi Dhi Na | Ti Na | Dhi Dhi Na |
Sign: X (1) 2 (3) 0 (6) 3 (8)

Dugun (Double) Layout:
| DhiNa DhiDhi | NaTi NaDhi DhiNa | DhiNa DhiDhi | NaTi NaDhi DhiNa |
Sign: X (1) 2 (3) 0 (6) 3 (8)

questions.question_text: Draft a biographical sketch of the legendary percussion maestro Ustad Ahmad Jan Thirakwa, highlighting his early training, associated gharanas, and his overarching contribution to the status of the Tabla. [80-100 words]
questions.answer: Born in 1892 in Moradabad, Ustad Ahmad Jan Thirakwa was arguably the most influential Tabla maestro of the 20th century. Trained extensively under Ustad Munir Khan of the Farrukhabad gharana, he successfully mastered and assimilated the distinct repertoires of the Delhi, Ajrara, and Lucknow styles. His famous nickname 'Thirakwa' was earned due to his playfully dancing, lightning-fast fingers on the drumhead. Through his crystal-clear tonal production, immense stamina, and balanced repertoire, he played a monumental role in elevating the Tabla from a mere accompanying instrument to a highly respected solo art form. He was awarded the Padma Bhushan in 1970.
